title: Chapter & Verse
description: A biblically rich round covering Genesis, the Kings of Israel, the Prophets, the Gospels, American landmarks, and history's greatest firsts.

questions.question: On the very first day of creation, God commanded this to exist, separating it from darkness.
God formed this first man from the dust of the ground and breathed life into his nostrils.
God renamed this patriarch from Abram to a new name meaning 'father of many nations.'
After wrestling with a divine stranger through the night, Jacob received this new name.
He sold his birthright to his twin brother Jacob for a single bowl of lentil stew.
Israel's first king, a head taller than his countrymen, was anointed by the prophet Samuel.
This son of David built the First Temple in Jerusalem and was renowned for his great wisdom.
When this king refused to lighten the people's heavy burden, ten northern tribes broke away to form their own nation.
This northern king married the foreign queen Jezebel and set up altars to Baal throughout Israel.
This young king of Judah found the Book of the Law during Temple repairs and launched a sweeping religious reform.
On Mount Carmel, this bold prophet challenged 450 prophets of Baal to see whose God would send fire from heaven.
When Syrian commander Naaman came seeking healing from leprosy, this prophet told him to wash seven times in the Jordan River.
King Darius threw this faithful young man into a lions' den for refusing to stop praying — and he survived.
Often called the weeping prophet, he recorded God's promise of 'plans to give you hope and a future' while Israel was in exile.
Exiled to the island of Patmos, this apostle received the visions recorded in the book of Revelation.
Jesus was born in this Judean city, laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn.
Jesus raised this man from the dead after four days in the tomb, in the village of Bethany.
After the Last Supper, Jesus went to pray in this olive grove before his arrest.
He stepped out of the boat and walked on water toward Jesus, but began to sink when he doubted.
At the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene at first mistook the risen Jesus for one of these workers.
Gifted by France in 1886, this copper statue in New York Harbor holds a torch of freedom.
questions.answer: What is the Statue of Liberty?

questions.question: Carved by the Colorado River over millions of years, this mile-deep gorge lies in Arizona.
The faces of four U.S. presidents are carved into the granite of this South Dakota mountain.
Completed in 1937, this iconic orange suspension bridge spans the entrance to San Francisco Bay.
questions.answer: What is the Golden Gate Bridge?

questions.question: Standing 555 feet tall on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., this obelisk honors the first U.S. president.
In 1903 at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, these brothers made the first successful powered airplane flight.
Alexander Graham Bell patented this device for transmitting voice over a wire in 1876.
In 1928, Alexander Fleming discovered this first antibiotic when mold accidentally contaminated his bacteria sample.
Marie Curie was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes — in physics and this second scientific field.
Jonas Salk announced his vaccine against this paralyzing childhood disease in 1955, ending a national epidemic.
